title: Graduate work options expand from 16 November
summary: A new 6-month Short-Term Graduate Work Visa opens for eligible Level 5–7 graduates who are not eligible for the standard Post-Study Work Visa. Level 7 graduate diploma PSWV eligibility also expands for eligible graduates who hold a bachelor's degree.
impact: Students choosing qualifications below degree-level routes need to re-check what work option their exact qualification creates.

title: Student maintenance requirement increases
summary: For applications from 30 November 2026, the monthly maintenance amount rises to £1,570 in London and £1,203 outside London, for up to 9 months.
impact: Students applying around the change date need to calculate funds using the rule that applies on their actual application date.

title: Graduate visa length changes for new applications
summary: Bachelor and Master's graduates who apply on or after 1 January 2027 receive 18 months on the Graduate visa instead of 2 years. Doctoral graduates remain at 3 years.
impact: Students comparing UK study for post-study time should plan around the Graduate visa application date, not only the course start date.

title: Student visa family inclusion rules tightened
summary: Most new Student visa applicants can no longer include a partner or dependent child unless an exemption applies. Family members also cannot later apply as subsequent entrants.
impact: Family plans now need to be checked before enrolment or major financial commitments, especially for taught-course applicants.

title: Bangladesh joined Études en France
summary: From 1 October 2026, students in Bangladesh can start their French higher-education application journey through the Études en France platform.
impact: Bangladesh applicants should build their application sequence around Campus France and Études en France instead of relying on older direct-process advice.

title: Family and post-study rules tightened
summary: For many third-country students in state-approved Bachelor and Master's programmes applying on or after 1 October 2026, the job-seeking period is generally reduced to 1 year and accompanying family rights are removed. PhD students are not affected in the same way.
impact: Application date now materially changes the family and post-study outcome for many Denmark-bound students.

title: Living-funds requirement increased
summary: For study-permit applications on or after 1 September 2026 outside Quebec, a single applicant must show CAD 23,448 for first-year living expenses, excluding tuition and transportation.
impact: Students using older CAD 22,895 figures may under-budget their study-permit financial evidence.

title: Student work is no longer generally unlimited
summary: Bachelor and Master's students whose residence permit was granted on or after 11 June 2026 are generally limited to 15 hours of work per week during semesters, with defined exceptions.
impact: Students should not use older advice about unlimited student work when planning income or choosing Sweden.
